claim: menu_driver() accepts an ascii character (HOWTO); it accumulates printable ASCII characters (Writing Programs)
quote: HOWTO: "an ascii character"; ncurses-intro: "accumulate printable ASCII characters"; menu_driver(3X): "printable character… checked according to the program's locale settings"; m_driver.c uses isprint(UChar(c)), not an ASCII-only test.
earlier: After only the HOWTO/intro wording I would have treated "ASCII" as matching those docs; the man page and isprint() show the real rule is locale printable characters.

claim: Example 21. Milt Columnar Menus Example
quote: Section heading "17.6. Multi Columnar Menus"; example title "Example 21. Milt Columnar Menus Example".
earlier: Seeing only "Milt" I would still call it a typo for "Multi" from the same section title.

claim: The Menu Basics listing frees only items 0 and 1 of five, and calls free_menu() on a menu that is still posted
quote: Five choices; cleanup is free_item(my_items[0]); free_item(my_items[1]); free_menu(my_menu); with no unpost_menu. free_menu returns E_POSTED if menu->status & _POSTED.
earlier: The listing alone already shows only items 0 and 1 freed while still posted; free_menu's E_POSTED confirms the second half.

claim: The Multi Valued Menus listing frees only items 0 and 1 of eight, and calls free_menu() on a menu that is still posted
quote: Eight choices (Choice 1–7 and Exit); ends with free_item(my_items[0]); free_item(my_items[1]); free_menu(my_menu); after post_menu, no unpost_menu.
earlier: Same conclusion from the listing before opening free_menu.

claim: The Menu Options listing frees the items before the menu
quote: HOWTO: unpost_menu; then free_item loop; then free_menu. free_item returns E_CONNECTED while an item is still connected; demo_menus frees free_menu before free_item.
earlier: The listing order alone matches the claim; E_CONNECTED shows why that order is wrong.

claim: The Menu User Pointer listing frees the items before the menu
quote: unpost_menu(my_menu); for (…) free_item(my_items[i]); free_menu(my_menu);
earlier: Same from the listing without the free_item man page.

claim: The Menu User Pointer listing stores the address of `MY_DATA data`, a variable local to the loop body, as each item's user pointer and calls through it after the loop
quote: Inside the for-loop: MY_DATA data = {func}; set_item_userptr(my_items[i], (void *) &data); later after the loop: data = item_userptr(cur); data->my_func(...).
earlier: No earlier source; the listing alone settles it.

claim: The list of menu options ends at O_NONCYCLIC
quote: HOWTO option list ends with O_NONCYCLIC. menu_opts(3X) continues with O_MOUSE_MENU after O_NONCYCLIC.
earlier: From the HOWTO alone the printed list does end at O_NONCYCLIC; menu_opts(3X) shows that list is incomplete.

claim: The mouse requests are quoted from an older menu_driver(3X), with its line breaks and soft hyphens (decora­tion), and without the double-click on an item
quote: HOWTO quote has "decora­" soft hyphen, older compressed wording, and ends at positioning the cursor on a click. Current menu_driver(3X) adds that a double-click on an item generates REQ_TOGGLE_ITEM.
earlier: The HOWTO excerpt alone shows the soft hyphen and missing double-click; the current man page confirms the omission.

claim: A link to text mode dos games at http://www.jersey.net/~debinjoe/games/
quote: HOWTO: "text mode … dos games" linking to http://www.jersey.net/~debinjoe/games/. Whether that URL is valid is outside the repository.
earlier: I can confirm the HOWTO prints the link; settling whether the link is wrong needs an outside fetch.

claim: the drive assumes it is an application-specific command
quote: Current man/menu_driver.3x: "the driver assumes it is an application-specific command".
earlier: Same: "drive" is not the wording in this tree's man page (it is "driver").

claim: menu_driver return one of the following error codes
quote: Current man/menu_driver.3x: "menu_driver returns one of the following error codes:".
earlier: Same from the RETURN VALUE line alone.

claim: replace a panel's window with a different window by calling `replace_window`
quote: ncurses-intro names replace_window; panel(3X)/panel.h export replace_panel, not replace_window.
earlier: Intro alone prints replace_window; the panel API shows the real name.

claim: The `stsdcr` window is a special case
quote: Intro: "The stsdcr window is a special case" then correctly says stdscr in the next sentence. panel(3X) discusses stdscr. menu_win.3x also still has the stsdcr typo.
earlier: stsdcr is already an obvious misspelling of stdscr before opening panel(3X).

claim: The `panel_update` code ignores hidden panels
quote: Intro says panel_update; the API is update_panels. update_panels walks the linked stack from _nc_bottom_panel; hidden panels are unlinked (IS_LINKED false), so they are skipped.
earlier: On the name alone I would still reject panel_update; the update_panels walk only confirms the intended behavior under the wrong name.

claim: You cannot do `top_panel()` or `bottom_panel` on a hidden panel()
quote: panel(3X) PORTABILITY: show_panel and top_panel "work equally well with displayed or hidden panels". top_panel calls show_panel; bottom_panel re-links an unlinked panel near stdscr.
earlier: From the intro alone I might have believed the restriction; the man page and implementations contradict it.

claim: Note that `wgetch` automatically calls `wrefresh`
quote: Intro states it unconditionally. curs_getch(3X)/lib_getch: wrefresh only if the window is touched or moved since the last wrefresh.
earlier: The intro's absolute wording would look right until the man page/source qualifier.

claim: For some reason the function `panel_hidden()` which tells whether a panel is hidden or not is not working, with a link to a 1999 bug report
quote: HOWTO asserts panel_hidden is not working and links geocrawler 1999. panel_hidden returns TRUE when !IS_LINKED(pan), FALSE when linked; panel(3X) documents that. The external report is outside the repo.
earlier: HOWTO's claim would stand until opening p_hidden.c / panel(3X).

claim: /* Update the stacking order. 2nd panel will be on top */ (also in the moving and hiding listings)
quote: Browsing/moving/hiding listings use that comment before update_panels(). new_panel places each new panel on top, so after panels 0,1,2 the third (index 2) is on top. update_panels does not reorder the stack.
earlier: The repeated comment matches the claim's presence; new_panel/update_panels show the "2nd panel on top" part is false.

claim: The program reads a panel's position and size from its PANEL_DATA when it comes to the top, but never writes them back, so a moved panel jumps back to where it started the next time it is moved
quote: set_user_ptrs stores x,y,w,h once. Tab reloads newx/newy/neww/newh from PANEL_DATA; move_panel uses those values but never assigns back into top->x/y after a move.
earlier: Same from reading the move/tab cases in that listing.

claim: "Show or Hide a window with 'a'(first window)  'b'(Second Window)  'c'(Third Window)", 83 characters on an 80-column screen
quote: That mvprintw string is exactly 83 characters.
earlier: No earlier source needed beyond counting the string.

claim: Mainpulate; is used to created panels; removes it form the stack; Entered Resizing :Use
quote: HOWTO prints "is used to created panels", "Mainpulate the panels", "removes it form the stack", and "Entered Resizing :Use Arrow Keys…".
earlier: Each fragment is already nonstandard English/spelling on sight (Manipulate/create/from).

claim: `bottom_panel` on a hidden panel()
quote: Intro forbids bottom_panel on a hidden panel. bottom_panel unlinks if needed then inserts above the stdscr pseudo-panel; it accepts a previously hidden panel.
earlier: Would have trusted the intro restriction before reading bottom_panel.

claim: In the `cbreak()` mode these control characters are interpreted as any other character by the terminal driver
quote: HOWTO attributes that behavior to cbreak(). curs_inopts(3X): in cbreak, interrupt/quit/suspend/flow-control characters are unaffected; raw is what passes them through uninterpreted.
earlier: HOWTO alone would support the claim; the man page swaps cbreak vs raw.

claim: `endwin()` frees the memory taken by curses sub-system and its data structures and puts the terminal in normal mode
quote: HOWTO says endwin frees curses memory. curs_initscr(3X): endwin restores modes/cursor/etc. but "does not dispose of the memory allocated by initscr or newterm"; delscreen frees SCREEN storage.
earlier: Would have accepted the HOWTO until the endwin memory note.

claim: `<curses.h>` also includes `<termios.h>`, `<termio.h>`, or `<sgtty.h>` depending on your system
quote: Intro claims curses.h includes termios/termio/sgtty. curses.h.in includes stdio/stdarg/stddef/stdbool etc., not those tty headers; MKterm.h.awk.in puts termios/termio/sgtty into term.h.
earlier: Intro alone matches the claim wording; the headers show it is about term.h, not curses.h.

claim: In linking with `curses` you need to have `-lncurses` ... There is no need for any other libraries
quote: Intro: only -lncurses. INSTALL --with-termlib splits libtinfo; example line shows -lncurses -lgpm -lncurses. Menu/form/panel apps also need their own -l libraries.
earlier: -lncurses is right for the base library; "no need for any other libraries" fails once termlib/gpm/panel are considered.

claim: To use ncurses library functions, you have to include ncurses.h in your programs
quote: HOWTO says include ncurses.h, then Example 1 uses #include <curses.h>. INSTALL default installs curses.h; --without-curses-h installs as ncurses.h instead.
earlier: The HOWTO's own hello-world include already undercuts "have to" use ncurses.h.

claim: `bool`: boolean type, actually a "char"
quote: Intro: bool is actually a char. curses.h.in typedefs NCURSES_BOOL from configure (@cf_cv_type_of_bool@) and may use <stdbool.h> or the C++ bool; INSTALL discusses matching C++ bool size/type.
earlier: Would have accepted "char" from the intro until the configurable bool typedef.

claim: `OK`: error flag returned by routines when things go right
quote: Intro calls OK an "error flag" for success. curses.h.in: #define OK (0); ERR is the failure flag (-1) in the same list.
earlier: Calling a success code an "error flag" is already wrong from the intro wording alone.
